title: P-256 sigma rho: top-limb distinguished test on the deferred-tests kernel

claims.statement: For uniform full-size P-256 Q=[x]P, the cold classical algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed H1 (extended to the small-key y-window adder table), M1/L-ori conditional fresh-exposure, H3 pricing and H-trail (average correction count per trail, with the fold model for dy) premises. Total charged work is at most 2^126.735049 units at C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions/unit. This is a conditional analytic bound, not an executed full-size attack. A=2^24, K=2^32, tau=0.4943092, residual Markov factor 400000, batches of 2^20 walks. Adders have Montgomery x in [2^192,2^231) and y within p/2 +- 2^-8 p, at most 2^40 fresh trials per adder with worst-case work charged. The deferred-tests field-step map is unchanged, but distinguished points now have canonical key < 2^196, theta=2^196/p, tested by one top-limb tst rather than extr and tst. Trail endpoints therefore change. The slot is (key >> 24) mod C, uniform on 2^172 inputs under M1 before reduction, and DP_MAX=2*ceil(S*theta)+2*K. The DP path skips the anchor comparison, as described in proof.md. The fix block preserves the canonical top limb through the y fix and re-runs the correct predicate. Three fixed/rare-path changes: (i) `finv` is 4-bit windowed (253 squarings and 39 multiplications instead of 255 and 127), saving 11,814 instructions per round; (ii) the 2^60 anchor cap is one `tbnz x12,#60`, so anchor rounds add 3*(2^20-1)+9; (iii) every unbatched rare-path addition shares `finv`, so F_MAX falls 41,190 -> 29,376 and wL 2,789,700 -> 2,021,790. Fixed plain work is charged 605,581,542 instructions per 2^20-walk round, plus 1,024 per round. C_COMMON is at most 577.577734, CORR at most 14.210693, total step charge at most 591.850860 instructions. The referenced branchy.json checkpoints are in the base submissions; this package omits that file for the 256 KiB limit. The shorter fix path receives no correction credit: xy_fix stays charged 47 against the measured 45, C_MAX stays 123, exits charged 13. Measurements are organizer-image emulated instruction counts, not production success evidence: both seeds show -(B-1) per round, anchors fall by the same amount; 2.4M compiled-tail cases agree with exact models. All preprocessing, failures, restarts, table initialization, lookup, transfers, replay, verification and output are included. Peak memory below 2^77 bytes, preprocessing at most 2^81.961192 units, zero nonuniform advice. Conditional success lower bound exceeds 0.39000025; the full production collision and correction premises remain heuristics. Inherited reduced-order experiments retain the old DP predicate and support only their disclosed scope, not the new production predicate. probability.md replaces the selected-merge tail by a 1.3e-6 all-abandonment envelope and derives report overflow from distinct first exposures; the small-failure bucket is 2^-59, not the old unallocated 2^-20. These use the shared per-class M1 environment, common-phase continuation, worst-case rare debits and first-duplicate termination.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the revised full production cost ledger (including the correction charge, its meter slack and abort term) and order certificate, then run the inherited complete reduced-order procedure, with checkpoint-only cycle detection and the small-key adder key rule at toy scale (adder_key_shift 2: adders redrawn until key < p>>2; shift 4 exceeded the runner's time limit; no y window), at tau=0.4943, the production value on its 0.0001 grid, retaining failures and replay checks. The two results have distinct scopes; neither establishes production mixing.
